description: Primitive canonical-CBOR encoding cases (RFC 8949 §4.2.1), independent of any Spindle artifact type — for validating a canonical CBOR encoder at the byte level.

cases.name: uint_0
cases.description: Smallest uint; fits in the initial byte.

cases.name: uint_23
cases.description: Largest uint that fits in the initial byte (additional info 0-23).

cases.name: uint_24
cases.description: Smallest uint requiring the 1-byte-argument form (additional info 24).

cases.name: uint_255
cases.description: Largest uint fitting the 1-byte-argument form.

cases.name: uint_256
cases.description: Smallest uint requiring the 2-byte-argument form (additional info 25).

cases.name: uint_65535
cases.description: Largest uint fitting the 2-byte-argument form.

cases.name: uint_65536
cases.description: Smallest uint requiring the 4-byte-argument form (additional info 26).

cases.name: uint_4294967295
cases.description: Largest uint fitting the 4-byte-argument form.

cases.name: uint_4294967296
cases.description: Smallest uint requiring the 8-byte-argument form (additional info 27).

cases.name: negint_minus_1
cases.description: Smallest-magnitude negative integer: CBOR major type 1, argument 0, logical value -1.

cases.name: negint_minus_100
cases.description: A negative integer requiring the 1-byte-argument form (magnitude 99, logical value -100).

cases.name: byte_string_empty
cases.description: Zero-length byte string.

cases.name: byte_string_short
cases.description: A short byte string.

cases.name: text_string
cases.description: A short UTF-8 text string.

cases.name: array_of_uints
cases.description: A definite-length array of three small unsigned integers.

cases.name: array_empty
cases.description: Zero-length array.

cases.name: map_key_ordering_by_length
cases.description: Map with keys "aa" and "z", constructed in that insertion order. Canonical order sorts by each key's own encoded bytes, so the shorter key "z" (1-byte header) is emitted before the longer key "aa" (2-byte header) even though "aa" < "z" lexicographically — this is the encoder reordering entries, not an input error.

cases.name: map_key_ordering_same_length
cases.description: Map with same-length keys "bb" and "ac", constructed out of canonical order; canonical order falls back to byte-lexicographic comparison of the key content, so "ac" sorts before "bb".

cases.name: map_nested
cases.description: A map whose value is itself an array and whose value is itself a map, exercising recursive canonical encoding.

cases.name: bool_true
cases.description: The simple value `true`.

cases.name: bool_false
cases.description: The simple value `false`.

cases.name: null
cases.description: The simple value `null`.
